_note: The SHARED FILES — the ones more than one spec is likely to want to edit, where 'who owns
this line' has to be answered by a declaration rather than by whoever committed last.
JSON takes no comments, so this is where this file is explained.
HOW IT IS USED. L-homes (soft) takes the files changed in the range, intersects them with
this list, and checks each one against the union of the 'home:' lines of the specs touched in
the same range (parseSpec in tools/gates/lib/spec-parse.mjs reads those). It REPORTS; it does
not block. A system that needs its own space gets its own module or its own screen with its
own home, rather than an edit inside somebody else's.
ENTRIES IS EMPTY, AND THAT IS A STATEMENT, NOT A GAP. As of 2026-11-01 this repository has no
spec files at all (docs/specs/ holds only README.md) and no commits, so no file has an owner
yet and nothing can be shared between owners. Declaring a file here before any spec names a
home would make L-homes report every edit of it against an empty union, which is noise, not a
finding.
WHEN IT STOPS BEING EMPTY. The first candidates, in the order they are expected to need an
entry: packages/core/src/index.ts (the core barrel every spec adds an export to),
apps/api/src/index.ts (the route table), apps/web/src/App.tsx (the screen shell). Each gets
an entry in the same commit as the first spec that names it as a home.
AND THE DECISION THAT IS REVISITED HERE, NOT IN SOMEBODY'S HEAD: L-homes is soft on purpose.
In a three-package monorepo a hard light on shared files would block ordinary work before
enough specs exist to have named homes, and a TypeScript merge conflict is visible by itself —
unlike a Unity scene, which is the case the Resonance original was written against. The
severity is reconsidered once this list holds more than ONE entry; until then soft is the
honest setting, and 'soft' is recorded in STANDING_LIGHTS in
tools/gates/lib/spec-parse.mjs, which is the one place a severity is declared.
ENTRY SHAPE, checked by manifestProblems() in lights/_shared.mjs:
{ "path": "<repo-relative literal path>", "why": "<one sentence>" }
A path matches an entry when it equals it or lies under it. No globs — see visible.json.
